title: The whole-group moment bound needs positive type and an identity bound
reason: For arbitrary admissible filling data the displayed conclusion has two additional analytic hypotheses. For β(s) the singleton second moment, the theorem takes a realization β(a⁻¹b) = ⟪u(a),u(b)⟫ and β(1) ≤ 2 dim_S, as well as Weil data on E. Mentioning a sieve for positive-type functions does not establish either hypothesis for β. They are proved later for a unitary amplitude-block realization in Moments.lean:571–577.
correction: State the conditional bound with its two assumptions and Weil data. When the operator realization is introduced, explain how it supplies them.

title: An amplitude-block realization must be unitary for equivariance and the total bound
reason: The chapter quantifies over an arbitrary representation, but the intertwining identity explicitly assumes that ρ preserves the chosen inner product. Its proof moves ρ across inner products. The whole-group Hilbert–Schmidt bound at line 567 and the good-forms theorem at line 1230 need the same assumption. Averaging the inner product on a finite group would change P* and the specified blocks.
correction: Introduce a finite-dimensional unitary ρ with respect to the inner product used for P*, assume admissibility and the requisite field data, and distinguish the block identities that hold before unitarity is imposed.

title: Qualify the Frobenius-element equivalence in the summary
reason: The summary claims that a domain alone identifies the Frobenius pair. Take p = d, n = 1, the residue field at a prime over d, the identity sign and v = ν_d. The two generator tests hold because σ_v sends ζ to ζ^d and √−d reduces to zero. But the pair (v, 1) cannot equal Frob_d, whose second coordinate is χ_K(d) = 0.
correction: State p ∤ q₁ for the two-generator test and p ∤ q₁d for the domain equivalence, as in lines 21 and 27.

title: Restrict the partner congruence in the summary to admissible exponents
reason: The unchanged summary asserts the congruence for any prime and exponent. For an odd inert p, take e = 0 and α = √−d. All the chosen places restrict to the same embedding of K, so the two sides are √−d and −√−d. Their difference is a p-adic unit because p is odd and p does not divide d. The lemma below requires e ∈ Iₚ° and α integral.
correction: Qualify the summary by “for e ∈ Iₚ° and integral α” and describe the partner as ν_{−pᵉ}τ, as in the definition.

title: The Schur expansion and jet comparison require compatible ranks
reason: The revised remark states the expansion for the arbitrary input and output ranks of the definition. With one place, input rank 2, output rank 1, and one height-one column, output truncation gives P_y=1. At y=0 every proposed input coefficient is a degree-one minor and vanishes, so the expansion would read 1=0. Both the expansion and the subsequent jet lemma assume FitsRanks.
correction: Require |n| ≤ |n′| and κ(τ,h)=0 whenever |n| < h < |n′| for both Schur conclusions. The definition of P_y itself allows arbitrary ranks.

title: A threshold for norm-one pairs alone does not give a cell rank
reason: The definition also requires the j-th leading minor to be nonzero and j to be the top rank exactly when the discriminant is nonzero. For example an isometry scaling the isotropic frame by 2, its dual by 1/2, and fixing the middle has a norm-one pair at z and at no earlier index. Its leading minor of size ϱ is zero since it preserves the isotropic span. The flag threshold therefore fails the cell-rank test.
correction: Describe all three tests for a proposed rank j, including one common norm-one coefficient for all a ≥ j.

title: The quotient identification with the positive space is linear
reason: The equivalence directly following the graph-isometry statement can be read as identifying the quotient with its inherited Hermitian form. At γ = 1 the quotient is A⊥/A and contains z of norm −N, whereas z⁺ has norm +N. The cited theorem identifies the kernel and range of a linear map. The isometry statement concerns the source and target obtained by exchanging coordinates of the link pair.
correction: Describe the induced E-linear bijection from the quotient, and reserve preservation of the positive form for the link isometry.

title: Unipotent invariance holds for leading principal minors
reason: The chapter says that minors are invariant on both sides. The minor theorem controls the top-left principal minor of each order. Adding an earlier column to a later one preserves these minors but can alter other entries and minors. The cell-stability deduction uses only the leading ones.
correction: Specify the leading principal minors of the frame Gram matrix.

title: The flag direct sum and rank formula need a primitive root hypothesis
reason: For a bare CM field the cited result does not give disjointness or the dimension formula. An existing cell rank and a zero discriminant give the ordinary sum at line 673. The disjointness at line 690 and rank formula at line 710 both assume a primitive 5040th root in E. With the zero-based frame of this chapter, the first j frame vectors span e₀ through eⱼ₋₁, so writing A_{≤j} without a definition also gives the wrong first summand at j = 0 on the usual inclusive reading.
correction: Assume the primitive root here and define the flag summand as the span of the first j vectors, empty for j = 0. A standing Weil-data hypothesis would also supply the root if its scope is made explicit.

title: Off-subgroup terms and remaining terms agree only after summation
reason: The excluded cosets in AvoidsScalarCosets are ζR̄₀ for nonidentity integral global norm-one ζ; the condition permits R̄₀ itself. For admissible data containing the requisite primitive root, the theorem identifies amplitude sums over each block. Terms outside both the Bessel subgroup and the remaining set with disagreeing characters have total amplitude zero by cancellation (lines 524–538). Disjointness of the cosets alone does not eliminate those terms individually.
correction: Specify the nonidentity global scalars, then say that at each allowed residue the off-Bessel amplitude sum equals the sum over the remaining terms by character cancellation.

title: Scalar cosets overlap the non-open part of the proposed partition
reason: Every scalar-coset element is non-open. In particular the identity lies in both categories. MomentBounds.lean:217–220 separates scalar cosets from their complement inside the full-fixer estimate. Only when a maximizing fixer omits a place does the proof split its elements into open and non-open parts (lines 477–510). Reading the three listed classes as a partition double counts.
correction: Describe the two cases for the maximizing set of places, with the scalar split in the full-fixer case and the open/non-open split in the proper case.

title: The first operator estimate uses an undefined residue set and a zero extension
reason: Ωᵢ appears without a definition. The sum is over residues agreeing with some member of R̄₀ in the other level-prime coordinate, and those residues need not belong to R̄₀. The immediately preceding sentence defines rψ only as a representation of R̄₀, so the difference in the displayed sum also needs its values outside that subgroup (zero by Moments.lean:169).
correction: Set Ωᵢ = {s ∈ Ḡ : there exists t ∈ R̄₀ with sᵢ₊₁ = tᵢ₊₁}, with the index modulo two, and extend rψ by zero on the complement of R̄₀.

title: Near-isometry is a lower mean-square estimate over subspaces
reason: The unqualified conclusion “almost an isometry with error 5b⁻⁴” suggests uniform two-sided control on vector norms. The statement bounds ‖ρ(e₀)P pr_U‖²_HS below by dim U − 5b⁻⁴ dim_S for every source subspace U. The allowance scales with the full source dimension, so this estimate can tolerate a kernel on a small subspace. The precise coefficient bound on each idempotent complement is Re((1−gᵢ)(1)) ≤ b⁻⁸/2.
correction: Describe the one-sided mean-square conclusion, and give the subspace estimate and coefficient threshold so that the error scale is unambiguous.

title: Conjugate the amplitude when reading off the Gram matrix
reason: With the stated convention the row-x, column-y coefficient is ⟨e_x,P_s e_y⟩ = overline(A_xy)/ν. The formula ⟨P_s e_y,e_x⟩ = A_xy/ν is correct for the reverse pairing. title: Project the first middle vector in the common-link summary

reason: The summary applies Υ to the moved-frame combination y in V. The input in Lean is Πγ(y) = y₀ + cρ z⁺ in P. For γ = 1 and the combination y = e₀, the ambient vector is nonzero and its input to Υ is zero.

title: Character disagreement gives vanishing for a stable sum

In the off-Bessel comparison only the disagreeing subset outside Γ* is discarded this way; Γ* retains every nonzero-discriminant element.

reason: The remark identifies Pₛ with the conjugated raw amplitude sum. Its block is the conjugate of A_all/ν, and the corresponding block of rψ(s) is the conjugate of A_Bessel/ν. Using the raw blocks makes the squared Hilbert–Schmidt sum ν² times the second moment defined earlier.

Taking the union over all d can enlarge the sum, and the proof gives no estimate for that union. The body has the correct order.

title: Name the intersection of the frame spans in the title
reason: Sharing a listed frame vector is stronger than having a nonzero intersection of the spans. For γ = −I the two frames f and −f have no vector in common as lists over the CM field, but their spans agree and the discriminant vanishes.
correction: Use “The discriminant vanishes exactly when the frame spans meet nontrivially.” The existing summary and theorem already specify the intersection.
